title: Reason Code 21: an NPS extension rejected the request (often the Azure MFA extension)
plain_english: NPS itself would have allowed the connection; an extension DLL registered on this server said no. On almost every modern NPS box that extension is the Azure MFA NPS Extension, so this usually means the MFA step failed: the user is not enrolled, denied or ignored the prompt, or the extension could not reach Entra ID in time.

causes.cause: The MFA challenge failed or timed out: user not registered for MFA, no default method, or the push was declined.
causes.next_check: On the NPS server open Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > AzureMfa > AuthZ and find the entry for this user at the same time; it names the exact MFA outcome.

causes.cause: The extension cannot reach Entra ID: expired extension certificate, proxy/firewall, or a tenant configuration change.
causes.next_check: Run the extension's health script (MFA_NPS_Troubleshooter.ps1) and check the certificate under the AzureMfa registry key has not expired.

causes.cause: The NAS gives up before the MFA push is answered, so the extension's reject races the user.
causes.next_check: Raise the RADIUS timeout on the NAS/VPN to 60 seconds or more with a single retry, so a phone prompt has time to be answered.
